checks.evidence: Action: Observe startup motion, inspect the rendered scene at 5 seconds and sought times 0, 17, 30, 73 and 120, and select each planet to compare its angle with its position and period. Expected: One sun and three differently sized/colored planets on circular, fixed-phase 12/24/48-second orbits. Observed: A large yellow sun and smaller cyan Mercury, larger gold Venus and intermediate red Mars rendered with circular orbit paths and different motion rates. At 0 seconds their angles were 0, 63.025357 and 126.050715 degrees; at 17 they were 150, 318.025357 and 253.550715; at 30 they were 180, 153.025357 and 351.050715; at 73 they were 30, 78.025357 and 313.550715. The visible locations followed those phases and periods, also after zooming out to see every body. Source index.html:11-13 supplies the matching sphere geometry, circular position calculation and periods; source constants alone were not treated as motion proof.

Action: Open a fresh desktop scene and repeatedly reload after snapshot edits. Expected: Initial time zero, 1x, running, no selection and overview, independently of saved snapshots. Observed: Fresh load was running at 1.00x with None, blank period/angle, disabled tracking and overview; subsequent motion was visible. Reload snapshots directly showed 0.0 or 0.1 seconds, 1.00x, PLAYING, None and Full-system overview while retaining saved observations. Ordinary loading elapsed time was not treated as a reset defect.

Action: Pause during the ordered tracking scenario, seek 30, wait during paused endpoint-speed probes, select planets and orbit the camera, then resume. Expected: Time and orbits freeze while paused and continue from that instant without a reset or jump. Observed: Paused 30.0 seconds and Mercury 180 degrees remained unchanged during the 3.1-second wait and speed edits. Equivalent paused probes at 31.7 and 44.9 seconds retained their exact angle readouts. Paused canvas selection and camera orbit/zoom remained usable. Resume from 30 at 2x began at 30.4 and advanced to 36.6 over the measured interval rather than resetting, and the rendered planets continued from the sought geometry.

Action: Set 0.25x, 2x and 4x both paused and playing, resume after each paused edit, and time each rate with only this scene open. Expected: No seek on speed change, stable paused positions and proportional motion with unchanged relative periods. Observed: Paused time and angle readouts were identical across every speed edit and 3.1-second wait. Playing samples were 30.1 to 30.8 in 3.103 real seconds at 0.25x, 32.2 to 38.4 in 3.103 seconds at 2x, and 45.7 to 58.2 in 3.105 seconds at 4x. After playing speed switches, samples were 30.9 to 31.7 in 3.102 seconds at 0.25x, 38.5 to 44.7 in 3.104 seconds at 2x, and 58.2 to 70.6 in 3.102 seconds at 4x. All were within preregistered tolerances, with visible orbital continuity and the same three angle/time relations documented in S1.

Action: Seek 0, 30, 120, 17 and 73 with the actual slider, revisit 30/17/73 after speed, playback and selection changes, restore a fractional 17.25-second import, and repeat 17 after reload. Expected: Seeking immediately pauses and deterministically updates all positions and information, with stable phases. Observed: Every seek paused at the requested time. The angle triples at repeated 30, 17 and 73 were identical to those in S1. With a fixed overview camera zoomed out to include all bodies, independently decoded scene screenshot pixels were exactly identical on revisiting each of those three times; image comparisons stayed in memory. The 17.25 import showed derived angles 157.5/321.8/255.4 degrees. After reload, live 17-second angles again read 150/318.025357/253.550715 degrees. Tracking sought positions also updated immediately.

Action: Seek 119, set 4x, resume across the endpoint, wait 3.102 seconds, seek 17 and resume again. Expected: Stop at 120 without wrapping or overshooting, then allow earlier playback. Observed: The first sample advanced from 119.9 to exactly 120.0 and changed to PAUSED with Mercury 0 degrees. The subsequent seek paused at 17 and resumed; a 3.104-second sample advanced from 17.8 to 30.3 at 4x without a reset.

Action: Inspect the loaded local Three.js dependency and scene implementation, then orbit and zoom the rendered overview and tracking cameras while paused and playing. Expected: Genuine Three.js 3D geometry with perspective and occlusion, not a flat imitation. Observed: HTTP resource timing listed the bundled three.min.js; its header identifies r160. Source index.html:11 creates WebGLRenderer, PerspectiveCamera and SphereGeometry. Actual drags changed orbit-plane perspective, body overlap and relative depth, while wheel zoom changed projected sphere sizes. Shaded sphere faces and sun/planet occlusion remained visible throughout those interactions.

Action: Capture paused Venus tracking at 30 seconds/2x, change every live field and resume, then capture while playing and inspect export/import/reload behavior and fractional imported angles. Expected: Stable unique nonempty IDs, every captured field and all three derived angles, no live-state mutation and no drift of saved values. Observed: Snapshot obs-mvgo9gqo-e876j displayed 30.0s, 2x, venus, tracking and 180.0/153.0/351.1 degrees. Its displayed values were exactly unchanged after moving live time to 17, speed to 0.25x, selection to Mars, overview and running playback. A later playing capture retained its captured 0.1-second instant and angle triple through reload while the live scene restarted. Captured IDs survived their exercised exports/imports or reloads, replacement captures had new IDs, and imported 17.25-second snapshots derived 157.5/321.8/255.4 rather than supplied angle values. Captures left live playback/selection/mode intact.

Action: The worker selected all three planets by native canvas while paused and playing, and by labeled buttons while paused; the parent then explicitly selected Mercury, Mars and Venus from the list during running 1x playback in a fresh 1440x900 scene. Expected: Both routes share visible highlight, selection and information in both playback states. Observed: Earlier canvas/paused-list routes selected all intended planets. The parent supplement recorded Mercury at5.8s with active mercury, period12s and Tracking Mercury; Mars at6.2s with active mars, period48s and Tracking Mars; Venus at6.6s with active venus, period24s and Tracking Venus. Every sample remained PLAYING, and transient screenshots showed the intended enlarged/brightened sphere at the tracking center with matching active list styling. The previously omitted playing-list clause is now observed, not inferred.

Action: Select all three planets, observe moving information, seek the fixed time matrix, and restore a null-selection overview after tracking. Expected: Correct selected name, period and rendered-position angle; explicit empty information and no highlight when unselected. Observed: Mercury/Venus/Mars showed 12/24/48-second periods and the angle triples documented in S1. Tracking Mars updated from approximately 256 to 294 degrees during the mobile playback samples while its rendered motion and information agreed. Restoring the null overview at time 30/speed1.5 cleared the previous selection to None, period and angle to em dashes, removed the selected styling and disabled tracking.

Action: Track Mercury, switch to Venus while playing, seek while tracking, and take three mobile Mars screenshots separated by two 1.6-second waits before switching to Venus and seeking 73. Expected: Target, highlight and information switch together, selected centers remain within 10% of the smaller scene dimension, and no-selection tracking is disabled without state change. Observed: Desktop Mercury and Venus stayed at the rendered scene center through the original scenario. Mobile scene bounds were about 351x361 CSS pixels; selected Mars stayed approximately at its exact center in samples at 17.3, 19.9 and 22.4 seconds, comfortably within 35 CSS pixels. Venus selection then changed the target/highlight/information without stopping 1.5x playback; seeking 73 immediately centered Venus and paused at 73. Startup and null-selection restores visibly disabled the tracking button.

Action: Return from selected tracking to Full-system overview in the ordered scenario and inspect overview at time 30 and on the 390x844 startup. Expected: A full-system view while preserving selection, time, speed and playback. Observed: State was preserved, but the standard desktop overview at time 30 omitted Mars beyond the right scene edge; at mobile startup near time 5 the left edge cut Venus and Mars was outside the scene. Manual zooming out could reveal all bodies, so this was a framing failure rather than a missing planet. Source index.html:14 changes only mode on overview, and index.html:11-12 uses a fixed distance of 11 without fitting the outer orbit to viewport aspect ratio. Not every possible tracking/manual-camera state was sampled; the observed full-system violation is sufficient to fail the group.

Action: Restore selected Venus tracking at 30/2x after unrelated live changes and manual orbit/zoom; repeat the restore. Import and restore null-selection overview at 30/1.5x after tracking, alter the camera and restore it again. Expected: Atomic saved state, paused playback, synchronized positions/information/target, deterministic standard tracking or full-system overview framing. Observed: Saved state and selection clearing worked; repeated tracking and overview restores returned visually matching standard orientations. However the restored null-selection overview at 30 seconds did not include Mars within the desktop scene, violating the required full-system standard framing. Source index.html:16 resets yaw/pitch/distance to .6/.45/11 regardless of aspect; the fixed-distance fit defect is visible after the actual restore. Repeated framing was visually compared, not independently quantified to a 2-CSS-pixel threshold; that missing precision does not erase the established full-system failure.

Action: Drag and wheel-zoom the overview and selected tracking cameras while paused and playing, including after restoring a snapshot. Expected: Both orbit and zoom operate around the current target without altering simulation state. Observed: Each of the four mode/playback combinations produced visible orientation and scale changes. Paused times and selected angles stayed fixed; playing states continued normally. Tracking retained the selected planet at its center during those camera manipulations. Restore returned the manual camera to its standard framing.

Action: Perform fast and slow cumulative drags beginning on the unselected Mercury at time 5 with Mars selected; the slow drag used 25 moves across 35 CSS pixels. Exercise planet buttons, sliders, playback/view buttons, snapshots and textarea/import/export at both sizes. Expected: Drags are not clicks, and DOM controls do not leak scene selection or camera input. Observed: Both drag samples retained Mars selection while changing camera orientation. Throughout the DOM interaction sequences, selection changed only by its intended selection/restore actions, and camera orientation changed only by intentional view, restore or scene gestures. The snapshot panel could change available canvas width through scrollbar layout, but no unintended orbital camera rotation was observed.

Action: Inspect playback, speed, selection, tracking, snapshot capacity and JSON feedback throughout both viewport sequences. Expected: Understandable purpose and state with coherent feedback. Observed: Clear Simulation/Planet selection/Observation snapshots/Snapshot JSON sections, explicit PLAYING/PAUSED and tracking labels, ID mapping and capacity/import messages made the tool ordinarily understandable. The speed slider thumb/value did not synchronize to restored speed even though the adjacent numeric readout did: restoring 2x left the control at 0.25. Very long unrounded live angles were noisy, and the quota capture feedback was misleading as detailed in D6. These are visible shortcomings rather than exceptional polish; rating 3 reflects an otherwise usable, coherent interface, not compensation for functional failures.

Deleting the middle observation retained A followed by the previous third entry. The new obs-mvgoa1ga-2vobg appended after them without collision and export preserved that order. Time17/2x/Mars/overview/paused was not changed by capacity, delete or capture. Mobile keyboard capacity rejection and subsequent successful capture after deletion also worked.

Action: At both actual viewport sizes, navigate with Tab and Shift+Tab and activate every primary DOM control using Enter or native range arrow/Home keys; edit the textarea using select-all/backspace and export/re-import through keyboard buttons. Mobile capture succeeded after keyboard deletion freed capacity.

Tracking centers remained easy to identify. The result was ordinary clear execution rather than exceptional visual communication. Standard overview clipping is evaluated in T4/T5, not an extra visual penalty here.

Action: Reload after valid import, deletion and capture; inject malformed and unsupported-version data only into observatory-snapshots-v1 and reload; fill a unique reviewer quota key using a bounded 8-MiB binary search, then capture through the real UI. In-memory playback, selection and restore remained usable. The filler was removed in finally and the exact original app-key absence restored before closing the scene. Storage read denial was not exercised; this does not negate the observed write-failure violation.
